thread:
alex: running into a typing headache with streaming endpoints + async iterators. runtime yields ChatDelta objects (pydantic model) but generated stubs end up as AsyncIterator[dict] or just AsyncIterator[Any]. pyright in the editor won't let me access `chunk.delta` without casts.

nina: which generator signature are we emitting? are we typing the async generator function itself or the returned object?

alex: our autogen client has something like: `async def stream_chat(...)-> AsyncIterator[dict]:` because we deserialize on the fly. But the pydantic model is ChatDelta. mypy is okay but pyright is noisy.

rafi: this might be the decorator problem. our `@retry` wrapper is typed as `Callable[..., Any]` currently and strips the async generator signature. That will force the stub to fall back to Any/Iterator.

priya: yep i've seen that. decorators need to preserve call signature types using typing.TypeVar/ParamSpec. We can update retry to be properly generic: `P = ParamSpec("P")`, `R = TypeVar("R")`, and then `def retry(f: Callable[P, R]) -> Callable[P, R]: ...` so AsyncIterator types survive.

alex: interesting. i'll try that. another wrinkle: even with ParamSpec the stub generator postprocess step normalizes streaming return types to AsyncIterator[Any] because we serialize pieces.

nina: could we annotate the returned stream type as AsyncIterator[ChatDelta] in the generated stub even if the runtime yields dicts then pydantic-constructs them? that would give DX the best ergonomics. But must be truthful to runtime — users might get raw dicts if they opt out of model parsing.

rafi: maybe generate two variants: `stream_chat_raw()` returns AsyncIterator[dict] and `stream_chat()` returns AsyncIterator[ChatDelta] (wrapper that does parsing). We actually do both at runtime in some endpoints already.

priya: another less invasive fix: in stubs, use `AsyncIterator[Union[ChatDelta, dict]]` which calms pyright but less ergonomic.

alex: for immediate workaround i cast the result: `stream: AsyncIterator[ChatDelta] = client.stream_chat(...)` then `async for chunk in stream:` works fine. Not ideal for newcomers in sample apps.

rafi: we should fix generator-decorator typing first, update autogen to preserve concrete AsyncIterator[Model], and update sample-apps to show the cast workaround or explicit var typing.

priya: i'll open a small PR to type the retry decorator with ParamSpec and add tests. also suggest a lint rule in devex sample apps to annotate streaming vars.

dev-bot: New issue created: #2378 "async stream typing: preserve AsyncIterator[Model] through decorators and stubs" (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/2378)

alex: awesome. can we also add a tiny pyright check in the generated-sdk CI that runs on a few sample apps? catches these regressions before onboarding docs break.

nina: agreed. adding to CI. thanks all.
